literal: Or the lord they served had died or been deposed.
idiomatic: Or the lord they served was dead or deposed.

literal: Though the documents of the time recorded their grades, as months and years passed everything was scattered and lost.
idiomatic: Records of the day were lost over the years.

literal: Only after many years would they seek to trace matters back; none failed to curry favor with one another and act as lip and teeth;
idiomatic: Years later, when records were sought back, everyone flattered one another like allies;

literal: they covered stains and hid flaws, recklessly applied vermilion and white, only aiming to gain a step in rank, with no regard for anything else.
idiomatic: they whitewashed faults and pushed promotions, caring only for rank.

literal: Even worthy and eminent gentlemen could not escape this affliction;
idiomatic: Even the worthy were not spared;

literal: for those below the middling, what more is there to say!
idiomatic: for lesser men, needless to say.

literal: Office was sought to complete one's aims, the person to secure one's standing—superior and inferior deceived one another; nothing exceeded this.
idiomatic: Men sought posts to finish their aims and bodies to secure standing; deceit between ranks was worst of all.

literal: Moreover, in diligently caring for the people's hidden woes, all responsibility fell on prefects and magistrates; their charge was not light and what was required of them was truly weighty.
idiomatic: People's grievances rested on local magistrates, whose burden was heavy.

literal: Yet when it came to their examination, all were bound by a six-year term; when the term expired they were replaced and returned, and only after another six years was advancement granted.
idiomatic: Yet their review used a six-year term, then six more years before promotion.

literal: Thus twelve years had to pass before one gained a single rank.
idiomatic: Twelve years passed for one rank.

literal: In the eastern and western two provinces, civil and military idle posts, scattered assistants in public offices, and superfluous officials with nothing to do—some answered a single duty only after several tens of days, or on the first and fifteenth merely attended a brief court.
idiomatic: In the two capitals' ministries, idle civil and military posts and redundant staff might answer one duty in weeks or attend court only on the first and fifteenth.

literal: When their examination day came, they again received a four-year limit.
idiomatic: Their review again allowed four years.

literal: Thus within one twelve-year cycle they could ascend three ranks.
idiomatic: In one twelve-year cycle they rose three ranks.

literal: Those, by real toil in heavy duty, found the road to noble advancement extremely hard;
idiomatic: Men in hard real posts found promotion very hard;

literal: these, by scattered posts and empty titles, found the way of ascent very easy.
idiomatic: idle title-holders found it very easy.

literal: How wide the gap between inner and outer, making thick and thin like this!
idiomatic: How vast the gap between inner and outer service!

literal: Mencius said: "Benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and faith are Heaven's nobility;
idiomatic: Mencius said, "Benevolence, righteousness, loyalty, and faith are Heaven's rank;

literal: dukes, ministers, and grandees are man's nobility.
idiomatic: dukes, ministers, and grandees are man's rank.

literal: The men of old cultivated their Heaven's nobility and man's nobility followed.
idiomatic: The ancients cultivated Heaven's rank and man's rank followed.

literal: " Therefore though culture and substance differed by age and rise and fall differed by era, none failed to treasure these name and vessels and not lend them to others.
idiomatic: Thus in every age they treasured rank and title and did not lend them lightly.

literal: Hence the statutes of reward and punishment were always strictly upheld.
idiomatic: Reward and punishment were always strictly upheld.

literal: Even in the Zhou's flourishing age, the five uncles had no office;
idiomatic: Even in flourishing Zhou the five uncles had no posts;

literal: in the Han's scrutiny, Guantao merely requested.
idiomatic: under Han scrutiny, Guantao only made a request.

literal: Truly, if reward and punishment were off by one degree, there would be no way to warn and encourage;
idiomatic: If reward and punishment slipped, there was no warning or encouragement;

literal: if supreme fairness were briefly set aside, covetous eyes would deceive one another.
idiomatic: if fairness faltered, men schemed against one another.

literal: Therefore they were most cautious and sparing, earnest to this degree.
idiomatic: Hence they were cautious and sparing to this degree.

literal: How much more when kin were not of one's flesh and blood, talent fell short of excellence, some filled a lone envoy's post yet from the start had no sweat-of-horse toil;
idiomatic: Much less when kin were not close, talent was slight, some held a lone envoy's post without battle toil;

literal: or spoke plans for increasing profit, yet in the end hung up an elevenfold gain.
idiomatic: or touted profit plans that ended as empty elevenfold gains.

literal: All inflated merit without achievement and falsely pointed to surplus;
idiomatic: All boasted false merit and false profit;

literal: sitting they gained several ranks of office and on the rolls became passably eminent nobles.
idiomatic: they gained several ranks by fraud and rose to visible rank.

literal: Thereupon crafty fraud sprouted, false argument flashed forth, they expended ten thousand schemes to seek glory and opened a hundred paths to chase profit.
idiomatic: Then fraud and sharp talk flourished; men spent endless schemes for glory and profit.

literal: Suppress it and the current had already passed; draw it out—what limit could there be!
idiomatic: Check it and the flood had passed; indulge it—where would it end!

literal: Zither and lute lie in necessary harmony; restring and seek the proper tuning.
idiomatic: Like a zither, government needs retuning to harmony.

literal: What is gone cannot be pursued; what comes may still be fit to change.
idiomatic: The past cannot be chased; the future may still be changed.

literal: According to the Zhou Offices: the Grand Steward's duty—at year's end he ordered each office to rectify its charge, receive its accounts, hear its accomplishments reported, and announce them to the king.
idiomatic: The Zhou Offices say: at year's end the Grand Steward had each office correct its charge, settle accounts, report results, and announce them to the king.

literal: Every three years he made a great reckoning of the officials' governance and rewarded or punished them.
idiomatic: Every three years he reckoned officials' governance and rewarded or punished them.

literal: I humbly think that today one might roughly follow that standard.
idiomatic: I think we might roughly follow that standard today.

literal: For those presently in office, at each year's end their home bureau should clearly distinguish months and days in post, fully verify ability and conduct, can or cannot, and examine real usefulness.
idiomatic: Each year every bureau should record months in post, judge ability and conduct, and note real usefulness.

literal: Then record their upper and lower grades; idle talk and grand speech—take none of it.
idiomatic: Record grades up or down; take no idle boasting.

literal: Submit lists to the Masters of Writing and review whether they fit.
idiomatic: Submit lists to the Masters of Writing for review.

literal: If there were error, correct and punish at once; one must not again push inquiry down and allow advance or retreat.
idiomatic: On error, punish at once; do not pass cases down and let men slip through.

literal: Once superior and inferior were fixed and good and bad divided, after memorial passed, the Merit Review Bureau should separately write on yellow paper and oiled silk.
idiomatic: After grades were fixed and memorialized, Merit Review should write separate records on yellow paper and oiled silk.

literal: One copy the home bureau's director and chief secretaries would seal and leave at the Gate Department;
idiomatic: One copy the bureau director and chief secretaries sealed and kept at the Gate Department;

literal: one copy the Palace Attendant and Yellow Gate would seal and keep in the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: one copy the Palace Attendant and Yellow Gate sealed and kept in the Masters of Writing.

literal: Seal it strictly; it must not be opened and viewed.
idiomatic: Seal it strictly; no one may open it.

literal: On the day of merit review, only then judge together face to face.
idiomatic: Only on review day should they judge together.

literal: As for inner and outer examination rules, that is not a matter for common handling; I beg broad discussion to make one standard.
idiomatic: Inner and outer review rules need broad discussion for one standard.

literal: If there were special plans and unusual policies touching rise or fall, discussed far and near with no dissent, one might of course weigh them at the time and not be bound by constant precedent.
idiomatic: Unique policies on which all agreed might be weighed at the time, not by fixed rule.

literal: As for appeals citing precedent streams, and requests greedy for glory and seeking rank.
idiomatic: As for precedent-chasing appeals and greedy requests for rank.

literal: If not limited by key and gate but allowed side passages at will, then creeping grass would be hard to remove, trickling streams would accumulate, defiling our great statutes and disturbing this great canon—I say they should be clearly forbidden to preserve perfect transformation.
idiomatic: Without strict limits, abuses would spread and defile the law; they should be clearly forbidden.

literal: An edict sent it out for broad outer discussion to make an everlasting model.
idiomatic: An edict sent it out for broad discussion as a permanent rule.

literal: In the end nothing was changed.
idiomatic: Nothing was changed in the end.

literal: At the time Liang Wudi's younger brother, Marquis of Xifeng Zhengde, came over in surrender; Baoyin memorialized: "Zhengde, being unfilial to kin, how can he be kin to others?
idiomatic: When Liang Wudi's brother Marquis of Xifeng Zhengde surrendered, Baoyin wrote, "Zhengde was unfilial to kin—how can he be loyal to others?

literal: If we release and wrap up this vicious villain and place him in the ranks, the hundred officials are the model—how can he be punished?
idiomatic: If this villain is seated among officials, what example do we set for punishment?

literal: Your servant's feud runs deep, pain coils the marrow, the road at dusk is far, and the day of revenge has no date—how could it be only about one petty fellow!
idiomatic: My feud runs deep and revenge seems far—but this is not about one petty man alone!

literal: Yet though talent is mediocre and near, the post is remonstrance and replacement; this foolish heart's inch of feeling—I dare not fail to state it.
idiomatic: Though my talent is slight, my post is remonstrance; I dare not stay silent.

literal: " When Zhengde reached the capital, the court treated him very coldly; after more than a year he rebelled again.
idiomatic: Zhengde reached the capital, was treated coldly, and after a year rebelled again.

literal: Earlier, Qinzhou city men Xue Bozhen, Liu Qing, Du Qian, and others rebelled, seized Inspector Li Yan, and pushed Moqi Dati as leader, styling themselves King of Qin.
idiomatic: Qinzhou men Xue Bozhen, Liu Qing, and Du Qian rebelled, seized Inspector Li Yan, and made Moqi Dati King of Qin.

literal: Dati soon died; his fourth son Niansheng usurped the title Son of Heaven, era name Tianjian.
idiomatic: Dati soon died; his fourth son Niansheng styled himself emperor, era Tianjian.

literal: He set up officials; made Xi Ahu crown prince, his elder brother Ani King of Xihe, younger brother Tiansheng King of Gaoyang, Bozhen King of Dongjun, and Anbao King of Pingyang.
idiomatic: He set up offices: Xi Ahu crown prince, Ani King of Xihe, Tiansheng King of Gaoyang, Bozhen King of Dongjun, Anbao King of Pingyang.

literal: Tiansheng led troops out of Longdong and then raided Yong Province, encamping at Heishui.
idiomatic: Tiansheng marched from Longdong, raided Yong, and camped at Heishui.

literal: The court was deeply worried; Baoyin was made Commissioner with staff, Western Route Mobile Secretariat, Grand Commander, and sent west on campaign.
idiomatic: The court made Baoyin commissioner with staff, western route commander, and sent him west.

literal: Emperor Ming visited the Bright Hall to give him farewell.
idiomatic: Emperor Ming saw him off at the Bright Hall.

literal: Baoyin with Grand Commander Cui Yanbo struck Tiansheng and routed him badly, pursuing to Xiaolong.
idiomatic: Baoyin and Grand Commander Cui Yanbo routed Tiansheng and pursued to Xiaolong.

literal: Advancing to attack Gaoping bandit chief Wan Qichounu at Anding, he again had a victory to his credit.
idiomatic: He advanced on Wan Qichounu at Anding and won again.

literal: At the time Tianshui man Lu Baidu and his brothers had first joined Niansheng in rebellion, then with his elder brother Zhongbao at Xianqin gathered troops to attack Niansheng.
idiomatic: Lu Baidu of Tianshui first joined Niansheng, then with his brother Zhongbao at Xianqin raised troops against him.

literal: Defeated in battle, he fled to Hu Chen.
idiomatic: Defeated, he fled to Hu Chen.

literal: Chen made Baidu Grand Commander and King of Qin, supplied him with troops and horses, and sent him back to campaign in Qinzhou.
idiomatic: Chen made Baidu grand commander and King of Qin, gave him troops, and sent him back into Qinzhou.

literal: He routed Niansheng's general Du Can at Chengji and again routed his King of Jincheng Moqi Puxian at Shuilo City, then reaching Xianqin.
idiomatic: He routed Du Can at Chengji and Moqi Puxian at Shuilo, then reached Xianqin.

literal: Niansheng led troops in person to resist and was again badly defeated.
idiomatic: Niansheng fought in person and was routed again.

literal: Baidu then turned against Hu Chen and sent his nephew Xinhe to lead cavalry east to draw the great army.
idiomatic: Baidu turned on Hu Chen and sent his nephew Xinhe east to summon the imperial army.

literal: Niansheng, pressed, then feigned surrender to Baoyin.
idiomatic: Pressed, Niansheng feigned surrender to Baoyin.

literal: The court praised Baidu's merit in upholding righteousness and made him Inspector of Jing and Duke of Pingqin.
idiomatic: The court praised Baidu's loyalty and made him Inspector of Jing and Duke of Pingqin.

literal: But Grand Commander Yuan Xiuyi and Gao Yu halted the army at Longkou and long did not advance west.
idiomatic: Grand Commander Yuan Xiuyi and Gao Yu halted at Longkou and would not advance.

literal: Niansheng rebelled again; Baidu was killed by Chounu.
idiomatic: Niansheng rebelled again; Chounu killed Baidu.

literal: Therefore the bandit power grew worse and Baoyin could not control them.
idiomatic: The rebels grew stronger and Baoyin could not control them.

literal: In the second year of Xiaochang, Baoyin was made Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Equal to Three Departments, Acting Great General, Director of the Masters of Writing, and given front and rear processional music.
idiomatic: Xiaochang 2 made Baoyin palace attendant, general of agile cavalry, equal to three departments, acting great general, director of the masters of writing, with full processional music.

literal: From Heishui at first to Pingliang at last, Baoyin faced the bandits year by year in attack; the bandits also feared him.
idiomatic: From Heishui to Pingliang Baoyin fought the rebels yearly; they feared him too.

literal: That Guanzhong was preserved was Baoyin's strength.
idiomatic: Guanzhong was preserved by Baoyin's effort.

literal: In the first month of the third year he was made Duke of Works.
idiomatic: In the third year, first month, he was made Duke of Works.

literal: The campaign had lasted long; troops and generals were worn; that month he was badly defeated and returned to Yong Province.
idiomatic: The army was worn; that month he was routed and returned to Yong.

literal: The authorities sentenced Baoyin to death; an edict pardoned him to commoner status.
idiomatic: The court sentenced him to death; an edict reduced him to commoner status.

literal: In the fourth month he was made General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Yong, Commissioner with staff, Western Expedition Grand Commander; from west of the Pass all obeyed his command.
idiomatic: In the fourth month he became general who pacifies the west, inspector of Yong, commissioner, western expedition commander; all west of the Pass obeyed him.

literal: In the ninth month Niansheng was killed by his King of Changshan Du Can; his whole house was destroyed.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Du Can killed Niansheng and wiped out his house.

literal: Can surrendered to Baoyin.
idiomatic: Can surrendered to Baoyin.

literal: In the tenth month he was made Director of the Masters of Writing and his old fief was restored.
idiomatic: In the tenth month he was director of the masters of writing and his old fief was restored.

literal: At the time east of the mountains and west of the Pass were filled with bandits; the royal army was repeatedly beaten north; hearts were discouraged.
idiomatic: Bandits filled Shandong and Guanxi; imperial armies kept losing; morale sank.

literal: Baoyin himself thought that campaigning for years had wasted expense on a vast scale; once overturned in defeat, he feared blame and suspicion and was inwardly ill at ease.
idiomatic: After years of costly war and one great defeat, he feared blame and grew uneasy.

literal: The court also was quite suspicious and obstructive.
idiomatic: The court too grew suspicious.

literal: When Imperial Censor-in-Chief Li Daoyuan was sent as envoy to Guanzhong, Baoyin thought he secretly meant to seize him and would have a different plot; he asked Hedong's Liu Kai.
idiomatic: When Imperial Censor-in-Chief Li Daoyuan came as Guanzhong envoy, Baoyin feared arrest and asked Liu Kai of Hedong.

literal: Kai said: "Great King, son of Qi Emperor Ming, is whom the realm looks to; today's move truly fits men's hopes.
idiomatic: Kai said, "You are Qi Emperor Ming's son and the realm looks to you; this move fits men's hopes.

literal: Moreover a rumor: 'Luan bore ten sons; nine sons were put to death, one son was not put to death—Guanzhong in turmoil.'
idiomatic: A rumor says, 'Luan bore ten sons; nine were executed, one was not—Guanzhong fell into turmoil.'

literal: ' King Wu had ten disorderly ministers; disorder means to govern—Great King should govern Guanzhong; what is there to doubt?"
idiomatic: King Wu had ten 'disorderly' ministers—disorder means to govern; you should govern Guanzhong; why doubt?"

literal: Daoyuan, traveling, reached Yinpan Post; Baoyin secretly sent his generals Guo Zihui and others to attack and kill him, then falsely collected Daoyuan's corpse and memorialized that white bandits had killed him.
idiomatic: At Yinpan Post Baoyin secretly had Guo Zihui kill Daoyuan, then claimed white bandits had done it.

literal: He then rebelled, usurped a great title, amnestied his territory, styled the era Longxu year one, and set up the hundred offices.
idiomatic: He rebelled, declared an era, amnestied his territory, styled Longxu year one, and set up offices.

literal: An edict ordered Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Mobile Secretariat Chief Changsun Chengye to attack him.
idiomatic: An edict sent Vice Director and Mobile Secretariat Chief Changsun Chengye against him.

literal: At the time Beidi's Mao Hongbin and his elder brother Xia led village righteousness to attack Baoyin.
idiomatic: Mao Hongbin of Beidi and his brother Xia led local levies against Baoyin.

literal: Baoyin sent his general Hou Zhongde to attack Xia.
idiomatic: Baoyin sent Hou Zhongde against Xia.

literal: Zhongde turned to plot against Baoyin; the army reached White Gate and Baoyin only then realized it.
idiomatic: Zhongde turned on Baoyin; when his army reached White Gate Baoyin realized it.

literal: He fought Zhongde, was defeated, took the princess and his youngest son with a little more than a hundred riders out the rear gate, and fled to Wan Qichounu.
idiomatic: Defeated, he took the princess and youngest son with a hundred riders out the rear gate and fled to Wan Qichounu.
